claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation in nanoscale FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers under sustained loading is governed by interface-mediated creep.
Severe lattice distortion at chemically complex interfaces lowers the energy barrier for dislocation nucleation and motion.
Short-range order at chemically complex interfaces lowers the energy barrier for dislocation nucleation and motion.
Enhanced dislocation nucleation and motion results in dislocation pile-up and strain localization that drives plastic deformation.
The starting multilayer consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The starting multilayer exhibits pronounced lattice distortion.
The starting multilayer exhibits measurable short-range order.
Interface characteristics will be varied while samples undergo sustained creep loading at controlled elevated temperatures.
Differences in crystallography and compositional complexity make the interfaces preferential sites for dislocation nucleation.
Differences in crystallography and compositional complexity make the interfaces preferential sites for dislocation accumulation.
Dislocation pile-up at layer interfaces promotes localized plastic flow across the multilayer.
More distorted or chemically inhomogeneous interfaces facilitate easier dislocation motion and faster progressive plastic deformation.
Samples with higher interface misfit will exhibit an accelerated creep rate relative to samples with more homogeneous interfaces.
Samples with higher interface misfit will exhibit a higher interfacial dislocation density relative to samples with more homogeneous interfaces.
High-distortion samples will show increased dislocation accumulation and localized plasticity along interfaces in TEM characterization.
Lower-misfit, lower-distortion baseline multilayers will deform more slowly and uniformly under identical loading conditions.
The proposed mechanism is limited to sustained loading at temperatures where creep is active while the nanoscale layered architecture remains intact.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when temperature or stress causes delamination or phase transformations.
